HLS Installer.874.exe DLL side-load from pirate-streaming ZIP lure AIInstallation High
Hunts the SilentCryptoMiner-fork delivery chain: the bundled legitimate 'HLS Installer.874.exe' executes from a user-downloaded archive and loads a same-directory rogue DLL, which then reflectively maps the encrypted main module. Targets the exact binary name and the user-writable parent folders (Downloads / Temp / Desktop) the lure ZIP unpacks into. Rationale: Anchors on the article's verbatim binary name 'HLS Installer.874.exe' (code block 1) and the user-writable archive-unpack locations where pirated lures land. Defender query joins process-create to image-load on the same PID to confirm side-loading rather than just an executed installer. Cross-checked NTT Security's 'chromium-patch-nightly' lure variant referenced in the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/ • https://github.com/SilentMine/SilentCryptoMiner
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate HLS-related video-tooling installers a user genuinely downloaded from a vendor
  • Penetration-test side-loading lab work mirroring this campaign
  • Repackaged streaming utilities downloaded from forums but not malicious
  • Security-research detonation of the sample in a controlled host
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has_any ("Microsoft", "Apple", "Google")) and InitiatingProcessTokenElevation != "TokenElevationTypeDefault"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the parent process and the source URL of the ZIP from DeviceFileEvents.FileOriginUrl/FileOriginReferrerUrl; hash the side-loaded DLL and check against IOC MD5s 6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73 / 7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f / 02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df. 2) Contain: isolate the device, quarantine the EXE+DLL pair under the unpack directory, kill any descendant miner processes. 3) Hunt: pivot on the DLL SHA256 across the fleet, search DNS for the article's .space C2 domains and the IP 107.172.212.235, look for the powercfg hibernate-disable commands and Defender exclusion additions described in the other UCs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
) on DeviceId, $left.ProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessFolder=FolderPath, ProcessCmd=ProcessCommandLine, SideLoadedDll=FileName1, DllFolder=FolderPath1, DllSha256=SHA2561
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 14d;
let ProcEvts = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "HLS Installer.874.exe"
| where ActingProcessName has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\");
let DllEvts = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "HLS Installer.874.exe"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".dll";
ProcEvts
| join kind=inner (DllEvts) on DvcHostname
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HLS Installer.874.exe Execution From User-Writable Path
id: c93f5b62-3a17-4f4a-9f1d-8c0f47b8ab21
description: Detects execution of the legitimately-signed 'HLS Installer.874.exe' binary used as a DLL side-loading host by the SilentCryptoMiner-fork distributed via pirated streaming and digital-library sites.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\HLS Installer.874.exe'
  paths:
    Image|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Desktop\'
      - '\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
  condition: selection and paths
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) @Image:(*\HLS\ Installer.874.exe OR *\hls\ installer.874.exe OR *\HLS\ INSTALLER.874.EXE) (@Image:*\Downloads\* OR @Image:*\Desktop\* OR @Image:*\Temp\* OR @Image:*\AppData\Local\Temp\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\HLS Installer\.874\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Desktop|Temp|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="HLS Installer.874.exe" (Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Desktop\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="HLS Installer.874.exe" (Processes.process_path="*\\Downloads\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Desktop\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
SilentCryptoMiner-fork: Defender exclusions added for %USERPROFILE%, %PROGRAMDATA%, %WINDIR%, .exe, .dll AIInstallation High
Detects the privileged preparatory step in the SilentCryptoMiner-fork chain: bulk addition of Defender path AND extension exclusions covering EXE, DLL, and the three root profile directories. The combination is unusual outside MDM / GPO baselines and is the campaign's defense-evasion fingerprint. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact exclusion targets (.exe, .dll, %USERPROFILE%, %PROGRAMDATA%, %WINDIR%). Requiring >=3 of the five exclusion strings within a 10-min window distinguishes the campaign's bulk-add behaviour from a single legitimate IT exclusion. Cross-checked MITRE T1562.001 and prior SilentCryptoMiner write-ups (Kaspersky 'Undercover miner' post referenced inline in the article). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/ • https://securelist.com/silentcryptominer-as-restriction-bypass-tool/115960/
ATT&CKT1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Endpoint-management tools (SCCM/Intune/JAMF) applying corporate AV exclusion baselines
  • Security software installers (other AV products) adding their own paths
  • Developer setting up a build-server exclusion path for self-signed binaries
  • Backup software (Veeam, Acronis) registering exclusion paths
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe", "MpCmdRun.exe", "ConfigSecurityPolicy.exe", "ccmexec.exe", "CcmEval.exe", "sense.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName — corporate MDM/Intune agents and ConfigMgr will appear here legitimately; anything else writing to Exclusions is suspect. Pull the exclusion set and look for the article's signature combo (.exe + .dll + %USERPROFILE%). 2) Contain: remove the malicious exclusions via Set-MpPreference -Remove, isolate the host, kill any process running from the now-excluded paths. 3) Hunt: pivot on the InitiatingProcessSHA256 across the fleet; cross-correlate with the MSRT-tamper, powercfg, and DNS-tunneling UCs in this pack — the campaign chains all four.
let WindowMins = 10m;
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions"
| where RegistryValueName in~ (".exe", ".dll") or RegistryValueName has_any ("%USERPROFILE%", "%PROGRAMDATA%", "%WINDIR%")
| summarize ExclusionCount = dcount(RegistryValueName), Exclusions = make_set(RegistryValueName), Bucket = bin(Timestamp, WindowMins), Actor = any(InitiatingProcessFileName), ActorCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceId, DeviceName
| where ExclusionCount >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
let WindowMins = 10m;
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Exclusions"
| where RegistryValue in~ (".exe", ".dll") or RegistryValue has_any ("%USERPROFILE%", "%PROGRAMDATA%", "%WINDIR%")
| summarize ExclusionCount = dcount(RegistryValue), Exclusions = make_set(RegistryValue), Bucket = bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMins), Actor = any(ActingProcessName), ActorCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine) by DvcHostname
| where ExclusionCount >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:*\Microsoft\Windows\ Defender\Exclusions\Paths\* OR @TargetObject:*\Microsoft\Windows\ Defender\Exclusions\Extensions\*) (@TargetObject:*%USERPROFILE%* OR @TargetObject:*%PROGRAMDATA%* OR @TargetObject:*%WINDIR%* OR @TargetObject:*\.exe OR @TargetObject:*\.dll)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| regex("\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows Defender\\\\Exclusions\\\\(Paths|Extensions)", field=RegObjectName)
| (RegValueName=/%USERPROFILE%/i OR RegValueName=/%PROGRAMDATA%/i OR RegValueName=/%WINDIR%/i OR RegValueName=/^\.exe$/i OR RegValueName=/^\.dll$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=RegValueName, distinct=true, as=ExclusionCount))
| ExclusionCount >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Exclusions\\Paths\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Exclusions\\Extensions\\*") (Registry.registry_value_name="*%USERPROFILE%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="*%PROGRAMDATA%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="*%WINDIR%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name=".exe" OR Registry.registry_value_name=".dll") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | stats values(registry_value_name) as exclusions dc(registry_value_name) as exclusion_count min(firstTime) as firstTime max(lastTime) as lastTime by dest user process_name | where exclusion_count >= 3
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Exclusions\\Paths\\*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\Exclusions\\Extensions\\*") (Registry.registry_value_name="*%USERPROFILE%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="*%PROGRAMDATA%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name="*%WINDIR%*" OR Registry.registry_value_name=".exe" OR Registry.registry_value_name=".dll") by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | stats values(registry_value_name) as exclusions dc(registry_value_name) as exclusion_count min(firstTime) as firstTime max(lastTime) as lastTime by dest user process_name | where exclusion_count >= 3
MSRT tampering: HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT DontOfferThroughWUAU = 1 AIInstallation High
Detects the SilentCryptoMiner-fork's MSRT-suppression step: writing the DontOfferThroughWUAU=1 policy value under HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT to block reinstallation, often paired with deletion of %WINDIR%\System32\mrt.exe via ZwSetInformationFile FileDispositionInformation. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact policy path 'HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT', value name 'DontOfferThroughWUAU', and the data value 1 used to block MSRT reinstall via Windows Update. Pairs the registry write with the article-described mrt.exe deletion under System32 (via ZwSetInformationFile/FileDispositionInformation) for higher fidelity. Cross-checked MITRE T1562.001 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ntifs/nf-ntifs-zwsetinformationfile
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT admin applying a corporate GPO that intentionally suppresses MSRT delivery (rare, usually scripted on a fleet)
  • Image-build / golden-image preparation script disabling MSRT before sysprep
  • Third-party patch-management product (e.g. Ivanti, ManageEngine) toggling WSUS-related policies
  • Legitimate WSUS migration script enumerating policy keys
Suppression filter
| where not(Actor in~ ("svchost.exe", "gpscript.exe", "gpupdate.exe", "WmiPrvSE.exe")) and not(ActorCmd has "GroupPolicy")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName — legitimate GPO writes come from GPSVC / WmiPrvSE; anything else (especially a side-loaded user-mode process) is high-confidence malicious. Confirm whether mrt.exe was also deleted (FileHit branch). 2) Contain: re-enable MRT by deleting the DontOfferThroughWUAU value, isolate the device, restore mrt.exe from a clean image, force a Defender update. 3) Hunt: pivot on the writing process SHA256, look for the Defender-exclusion UC and powercfg hibernate-disable UC on the same host within +/-10 minutes — they're the same chain.
let Lookback = 14d;
let RegHit = DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet", "RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "DontOfferThroughWUAU"
| where tostring(RegistryValueData) in ("1", "0x1", "0x00000001")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Actor=InitiatingProcessFileName, ActorCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_PolicyReg";
let FileHit = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Lookback)
| where ActionType in ("FileDeleted", "FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has @"\System32\" and FileName =~ "mrt.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Actor=InitiatingProcessFileName, ActorCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_FileDelete";
union RegHit, FileHit
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 14d;
let RegHit = ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where RegistryKey has @"\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT"
| where RegistryValue =~ "DontOfferThroughWUAU"
| where tostring(RegistryValueData) in ("1", "0x1", "0x00000001")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Actor=ActingProcessName, ActorCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_PolicyReg";
let FileHit = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Lookback)
| where EventType in ("FileDeleted", "FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\System32\"
| where TargetFileName =~ "mrt.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Actor=ActingProcessName, ActorCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Signal="MRT_FileDelete";
union RegHit, FileHit
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: MSRT Suppression via DontOfferThroughWUAU Policy Key
id: 7b41f02e-25a1-4b3c-b86a-92e0f5f2c5a4
description: Detects creation of the HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT\DontOfferThroughWUAU=1 registry value used by the SilentCryptoMiner-fork distributed via pirated streaming sites to prevent reinstallation of the Microsoft Malicious Software Removal Tool.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.t1112
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|contains: '\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT\DontOfferThroughWUAU'
    Details:
      - 'DWORD (0x00000001)'
      - '1'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:*\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT\DontOfferThroughWUAU OR @TargetObject:*\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\MRT\DontOfferThroughWUAU) (@Details:*0x00000001* OR @Details:"DWORD (0x00000001)" OR @Details:1)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\MRT/i
| RegValueName=/DontOfferThroughWUAU/i
| RegStringValue=/^(1|0x1|0x00000001)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\MRT*" Registry.registry_value_name="DontOfferThroughWUAU" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\Software\\Policies\\Microsoft\\MRT*" Registry.registry_value_name="DontOfferThroughWUAU" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.process_name Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
powercfg sleep/hibernate disable burst (4-command sequence) AIInstallation High
Detects the SilentCryptoMiner-fork's miner-uptime preparation: four powercfg commands disabling hibernate AC, hibernate DC, standby AC, and standby DC in rapid succession. The four-command burst from a single non-administrative parent is the campaign signature distinguishing miners from legitimate power-management tweaks. Rationale: Anchors on the four verbatim powercfg arguments from the article (table 2: hibernate-timeout-ac/dc, standby-timeout-ac/dc, all set to 0). Requiring >=3 distinct variants in a 5-min window separates the miner's burst from a sysadmin tweaking a single setting. The /x form in the article is also alternative-matched. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Laptop-power-profile tuning by IT during desktop standardisation
  • Kiosk / digital-signage build script disabling all sleep states
  • Citrix/VDI gold-image preparation scripts
  • Mining-rig-like legitimate workloads (rendering farm, ML training boxes) configured by their owners
Suppression filter
| where not(Parent in~ ("gpscript.exe", "ccmexec.exe", "MsSense.exe", "sysprep.exe", "setupcl.exe")) and not(ParentCmd has_any ("GroupPolicy", "Intune", "ConfigMgr"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: check the parent process — Group Policy / SCCM /Intune scripts are legitimate; user-shell or unknown binaries running this from %TEMP%/%USERPROFILE% are not. Pull the parent SHA256. 2) Contain: re-enable power-saving with the corporate profile, isolate if the parent is unsigned/untrusted, kill any high-CPU processes running from user-writable paths. 3) Hunt: cross-correlate with the Defender-exclusion and MSRT-tamper UCs on the same host within +/-15 minutes; pivot on parent process SHA256 across the fleet and search for outbound traffic to 107.172.212.235 or the .space C2 domains.
let WindowMins = 5m;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "powercfg.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-hibernate-timeout-ac 0", "-hibernate-timeout-dc 0", "-standby-timeout-ac 0", "-standby-timeout-dc 0", "/x -hibernate-timeout", "/x -standby-timeout")
| extend Flag = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-ac", "hib_ac",
    ProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-dc", "hib_dc",
    ProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-ac", "sby_ac",
    ProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-dc", "sby_dc",
    "other")
| summarize Variants = dcount(Flag), Cmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine), Parent = any(InitiatingProcessFileName), ParentCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), Bucket = bin(Timestamp, WindowMins) by DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName
| where Variants >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
let WindowMins = 5m;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "powercfg.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-hibernate-timeout-ac 0", "-hibernate-timeout-dc 0", "-standby-timeout-ac 0", "-standby-timeout-dc 0", "/x -hibernate-timeout", "/x -standby-timeout")
| extend Flag = case(
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-ac", "hib_ac",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "hibernate-timeout-dc", "hib_dc",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-ac", "sby_ac",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "standby-timeout-dc", "sby_dc",
    "other")
| summarize Variants = dcount(Flag), Cmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine), Parent = any(ParentProcessName), ParentCmd = any(ParentProcessCommandLine), Bucket = bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMins) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| where Variants >= 3
| order by Bucket desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@Image:*\powercfg.exe OR @Image:*\POWERCFG.EXE) (@CommandLine:*-hibernate-timeout-ac\ 0* OR @CommandLine:*-hibernate-timeout-dc\ 0* OR @CommandLine:*-standby-timeout-ac\ 0* OR @CommandLine:*-standby-timeout-dc\ 0*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\powercfg\.exe$/i
| regex("-(hibernate|standby)-timeout-(ac|dc)\\s+0", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName], function=count(field=CommandLine, distinct=true, as=Variants))
| Variants >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count values(Processes.process) as commands min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="powercfg.exe" (Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-dc*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-dc*0*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 3
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as commands min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="powercfg.exe" (Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-hibernate-timeout-dc*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-ac*0*" OR Processes.process="*-standby-timeout-dc*0*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 3
SilentCryptoMiner DNS tunneling to *.microsoft.com lookalike and known C2 .space domains AICommand & Control High
Hunts the article's specific C2 channel: DNS queries to lookalike domains ending in 'microsoft.com' but resolving to non-Microsoft IPs, plus direct queries to the article's six .space/.online IOC domains. The DNS-tunneled fingerprint payload (CPU info, C: serial, elevation flag, start time) is encoded into a single large subdomain label. Rationale: Anchors on the article's eight IOC domains, the IP 107.172.212.235, and the described DNS-tunneling pattern of long subdomain labels under *.microsoft.com whose A-record resolution falls outside Microsoft's published ranges. The query unions the high-confidence IOC branch with the heuristic tunneling branch so legacy unsubmitted-IP detections and known-IOC detections share one rule. Cross-checked MITRE T1071.004 / T1572 mappings. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/ • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/urls-and-ip-address-ranges
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1572
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Microsoft Edge / Office DNS queries to obscure microsoft.com subdomains during product telemetry
  • Long DNS queries by Microsoft Defender ASR/MAPS to *.microsoft.com edge nodes (different IP range)
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonations of the sample inside the corporate network
  • An MS partner CDN node briefly resolved to a non-MS range during a DNS infra failover
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","OfficeClickToRun.exe","MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull ContextImageFileName / InitiatingProcessFileName — if a non-browser non-MS-signed process is making the resolution, treat as confirmed. Hash the binary and check against the three article MD5s. 2) Contain: sinkhole the eight IOC domains and block 107.172.212.235 at the perimeter; isolate the host; collect a memory image (the main module reflectively loads, so the on-disk DLL alone is insufficient for forensics). 3) Hunt: pivot on the same writing process across the fleet, look back 90 days for the file.ipfs.us.69.mu legacy domain, correlate with the Defender-exclusion / MSRT-tamper / powercfg UCs in this pack — they're the same chain.
let CampaignDomains = dynamic(["urush1bar4.online","file.ipfs.us.69.mu","5d14vnfb.space","r7mvjl67.space","zgj1tam9.space","jeaw520i.space","qdmagva5.space","m4yuri.online"]);
let CampaignIp = "107.172.212.235";
let IocHit = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where (isnotempty(RemoteUrl) and RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignDomains)) or RemoteIP == CampaignIp
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, Signal="IOC_Hit";
let TunnelHit = DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse" or ActionType has "Dns"
| where RemoteUrl endswith ".microsoft.com"
| extend QueryLen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where QueryLen > 80
| where not(RemoteIP startswith "13." or RemoteIP startswith "20." or RemoteIP startswith "23." or RemoteIP startswith "40." or RemoteIP startswith "52." or RemoteIP startswith "104." or RemoteIP startswith "131.107." or RemoteIP startswith "134.170." or RemoteIP startswith "137.116." or RemoteIP startswith "157.55." or RemoteIP startswith "168.61." or RemoteIP startswith "191.236." or RemoteIP startswith "207.46.")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, Signal="DNS_Tunnel_MSLookalike";
union IocHit, TunnelHit
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignDomains = dynamic(["urush1bar4.online","file.ipfs.us.69.mu","5d14vnfb.space","r7mvjl67.space","zgj1tam9.space","jeaw520i.space","qdmagva5.space","m4yuri.online"]);
let CampaignIp = "107.172.212.235";
let MsRanges = dynamic(["13.","20.","23.","40.","52.","104.","131.107.","134.170.","137.116.","157.55.","168.61.","191.236.","207.46."]);
let IocHit = ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (CampaignDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr, Signal="IOC_Hit";
let TunnelHit = ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DnsQuery endswith ".microsoft.com"
| extend QueryLen = strlen(DnsQuery)
| where QueryLen > 80
| extend InMsRange = iff(isnotempty(DstIpAddr) and (DstIpAddr startswith "13." or DstIpAddr startswith "20." or DstIpAddr startswith "23." or DstIpAddr startswith "40." or DstIpAddr startswith "52." or DstIpAddr startswith "104." or DstIpAddr startswith "131.107." or DstIpAddr startswith "134.170." or DstIpAddr startswith "137.116." or DstIpAddr startswith "157.55." or DstIpAddr startswith "168.61." or DstIpAddr startswith "191.236." or DstIpAddr startswith "207.46."), true, false)
| where InMsRange == false
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr, Signal="DNS_Tunnel_MSLookalike";
union IocHit, TunnelHit
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SilentCryptoMiner-Fork C2 Domains and IP Resolution
id: 2ad6f719-3f7c-4d05-9c5f-7e0f7d1a3c98
description: Detects DNS resolutions / network connections to the SilentCryptoMiner-fork campaign indicators distributed via pirated streaming and digital-library sites in 2026.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.t1071.004
  - attack.t1572
logsource:
  category: dns
  product: windows
detection:
  domains:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - 'urush1bar4.online'
      - 'file.ipfs.us.69.mu'
      - '5d14vnfb.space'
      - 'r7mvjl67.space'
      - 'zgj1tam9.space'
      - 'jeaw520i.space'
      - 'qdmagva5.space'
      - 'm4yuri.online'
  condition: domains
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.syslog OR windows.security) (@DestinationHostname:(*urush1bar4.online OR *file.ipfs.us.69.mu OR *5d14vnfb.space OR *r7mvjl67.space OR *zgj1tam9.space OR *jeaw520i.space OR *qdmagva5.space OR *m4yuri.online) OR @QueryName:(*urush1bar4.online OR *file.ipfs.us.69.mu OR *5d14vnfb.space OR *r7mvjl67.space OR *zgj1tam9.space OR *jeaw520i.space OR *qdmagva5.space OR *m4yuri.online) OR @DestinationIp:107.172.212.235)
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest OR #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4)
| (DomainName=/(urush1bar4\.online|file\.ipfs\.us\.69\.mu|5d14vnfb\.space|r7mvjl67\.space|zgj1tam9\.space|jeaw520i\.space|qdmagva5\.space|m4yuri\.online)$/i OR RemoteAddressIP4="107.172.212.235")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="*.5d14vnfb.space" OR DNS.query="*.r7mvjl67.space" OR DNS.query="*.zgj1tam9.space" OR DNS.query="*.jeaw520i.space" OR DNS.query="*.qdmagva5.space" OR DNS.query="*.m4yuri.online" OR DNS.query="*.urush1bar4.online" OR DNS.query="file.ipfs.us.69.mu") by DNS.src DNS.dest DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*.microsoft.com" by DNS.src DNS.dest DNS.query DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | eval qlen=len(query) | where qlen > 80 AND NOT match(answer,"^(13\.|20\.|23\.|40\.|52\.|104\.|131\.107\.|134\.170\.|137\.116\.|157\.55\.|168\.61\.|191\.236\.|207\.46\.)")]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="*.5d14vnfb.space" OR DNS.query="*.r7mvjl67.space" OR DNS.query="*.zgj1tam9.space" OR DNS.query="*.jeaw520i.space" OR DNS.query="*.qdmagva5.space" OR DNS.query="*.m4yuri.online" OR DNS.query="*.urush1bar4.online" OR DNS.query="file.ipfs.us.69.mu") by DNS.src DNS.dest DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query="*.microsoft.com" by DNS.src DNS.dest DNS.query DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | eval qlen=len(query) | where qlen > 80 AND NOT match(answer,"^(13\.|20\.|23\.|40\.|52\.|104\.|131\.107\.|134\.170\.|137\.116\.|157\.55\.|168\.61\.|191\.236\.|207\.46\.)")]
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",

| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or SHA1 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or MD5 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or SHA1 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df") or MD5 in~ ("6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db73", "7f624407ae489324e96a708a09c17e6f", "02a43b3423367b9dddc24cc7dfc070df"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| where (FolderPath has_any ("C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome", "%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Roaming\Sandboxie") or FileName in~ ("installer.874.exe", "mrt.exe", "conhost.exe", ".ftp.sh"))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

// Registry persistence locations named in the article
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any ("HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\MRT")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Hazy Scorpius (CL0P) Oracle EBS exploitation via CVE-2025-61882 — concurrent processing spawns shell/wget · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud npm postinstall reads cloud credential files (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.kube, gcloud ADC) · [LLM] Bling Libra: Entra device join immediately after vishing-driven MFA registration
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud exfiltration: node.exe POSTs to api.github.com creating public repo · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Shai-Hulud npm postinstall reads cloud credential files (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.kube, gcloud ADC) AIInstallation High
Hunts the Shai-Hulud worm's secret-harvesting stage: a node/npm/yarn process opens AWS credentials, SSH private keys, Kubernetes kubeconfig, or GCP application-default-credentials. The article confirms TGR-CRI-1135 released an open-source version on 2026-05-13, so copycats will reuse this file-access pattern. Rationale: Article confirms TGR-CRI-1135's malware exfiltrates 'cloud access tokens, SSH keys, Kubernetes secrets' and announced the open-source Shai-Hulud release 2026-05-13. Datadog Security Labs and Unit 42 follow-up writeups confirm the exact filesystem paths (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/, ~/.kube/config, application_default_credentials.json) and that node is the executing host — making this a precise file-access pivot, not a generic 'credentials in files' rule. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/ctrl-tinycolor-and-40-npm-packages-compromised
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1195.002 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI build agents (Jenkins, GitHub Actions self-hosted runners) where node legitimately reads ~/.aws/credentials for terraform/aws-cdk deploys
  • Developer laptops running aws-sdk-based scripts that hydrate from the shared credentials file
  • kubectl-node helper plugins (kubeseal, kubectl-krew node wrappers) opening ~/.kube/config
  • npm packages such as @kubernetes/client-node initialising from default kubeconfig
  • Backup tools written in node reading SSH keys for rsync-over-ssh wrappers
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("terraform.exe","cdk.exe","aws.exe","kubectl.exe","helm.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("aws-cdk","@kubernetes/client-node","terraform-provider"))
| where not (DeviceName matches regex @"(?i)(jenkins|gha-runner|build-agent)")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree for the offending node PID — confirm parent is npm/yarn/pnpm install (vs an IDE or aws-cdk). Get the package.json / npm-debug.log on the host; identify the package + version executing postinstall. Check DeviceNetworkEvents for the same node PID hitting api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, webhook.site, or 169.254.169.254 (cloud IMDS). 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response, rotate ALL credentials present in the touched files (AWS access keys, SSH keys, kubeconfig tokens, GCP service-account JSON), revoke any GitHub PATs the user has. 3) Hunt: pivot on the package name across all DevEnv/CI hosts (`DeviceProcessEvents | where ProcessCommandLine has "<pkg>"`); search for newly-created public GitHub repos owned by impacted users with description containing 'Sha1-Hulud' or 'Shai-Hulud'; scan CloudTrail for `GetSecretValue` / `sts:GetCallerIdentity` from any compromised key.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","yarn","pnpm.exe","pnpm")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @"\.ssh\id_rsa", @"/.ssh/id_rsa", @"\.ssh\id_ed25519", @"/.ssh/id_ed25519", @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config", @"application_default_credentials.json", @"\gcloud\credentials.db")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileAccessed")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe)?$" or ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)$"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(\.aws[\\/]credentials|\.ssh[\\/]id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|\.kube[\\/]config|application_default_credentials\.json|gcloud[\\/]credentials\.db)"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Shai-Hulud npm Worm Reads Cloud Credential Files
id: 9c4a1e62-1f0b-4b3a-8f3d-c7f1b3b8d401
status: experimental
description: Detects node/npm/yarn/pnpm processes accessing AWS, SSH, Kubernetes or GCP credential files — the Shai-Hulud worm's credential-harvest stage. TGR-CRI-1135 open-sourced the tool 2026-05-13.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cyber-extortion-economy/
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/
  - https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/28
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: file_access
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
  selection_file:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.aws\credentials'
      - '\.ssh\id_rsa'
      - '\.ssh\id_ed25519'
      - '\.kube\config'
      - 'application_default_credentials.json'
      - '\gcloud\credentials.db'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_file
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate IaC tooling (terraform-wrapped node helpers, cdktf) reading AWS profile
  - Developer-machine kube/aws CLI plugin that legitimately shells out to node
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\npm.exe OR *\NPM.EXE OR *\yarn.exe OR *\YARN.EXE OR *\pnpm.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\.aws\credentials OR *\.ssh\id_rsa* OR *\.ssh\id_ed25519* OR *\.kube\config OR *application_default_credentials.json OR *\gcloud\credentials.db)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)\.exe$/i
| regex("(\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|\\\\\\.ssh\\\\id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|\\\\\\.kube\\\\config|application_default_credentials\\.json|\\\\gcloud\\\\credentials\\.db)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
| _count > 0
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","yarn","pnpm.exe","pnpm")) AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*application_default_credentials.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\gcloud\\credentials.db") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","yarn","pnpm.exe","pnpm")) AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_rsa*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config" OR Filesystem.file_path="*application_default_credentials.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\gcloud\\credentials.db") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Shai-Hulud exfiltration: node.exe POSTs to api.github.com creating public repo AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Shai-Hulud worm's exfiltration channel — a node/npm process making API calls to api.github.com on a non-developer host (or burst of repo-creation API traffic). The worm dumps stolen secrets into a newly-created public GitHub repo tagged 'Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming'. Rationale: Article ties TGR-CRI-1135 (Shai-Hulud author) to the open-source release on 2026-05-13. Datadog Security Labs and Unit 42 confirm exfil channel is a public GitHub repo created via api.github.com — pairing the credential-file read (UC1) with an outbound github.com call from the same node PID inside 10 minutes is high-fidelity vs background developer noise. Cross-checked against: • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.upwind.io/feed/shai-hulud-2-npm-supply-chain-worm-attack • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1102 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine `npm publish` or `gh release create` workflows from developer laptops
  • CI runners using @octokit/rest to update repo metadata as part of release pipelines
  • Renovate / Dependabot agents reading project files then posting PRs via the GitHub API
  • semantic-release postinstall hooks that legitimately touch ~/.npmrc + github.com
  • Internal package registries proxied through api.github.com Enterprise
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@octokit","semantic-release","gh release","renovate","dependabot")) and not (DeviceName matches regex @"(?i)(jenkins|gha-runner|build-agent|renovate)")
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the HTTP body size of POSTs from the offending node PID — Shai-Hulud uploads double-base64-encoded blobs ~kB-MB range. Run `gh api /users/<user>/repos --paginate` and look for repos created in the last 24h whose description matches 'Shai-Hulud' / 'Sha1-Hulud' / contains the package@version string. 2) Contain: revoke all GitHub PATs / fine-grained tokens for the user, force-rotate the AWS/GCP/k8s creds touched in UC1, delete the exfil repo via GitHub Support (it's already harvested but limits secondary use). 3) Hunt: correlate with UC1 hits across the org; query GitHub audit log for `repo.create` events authored by tokens issued from compromised endpoints; sweep TruffleHog over the GitHub Enterprise org for posted secrets.
let creds = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials", @"\.ssh\id_", @"/.ssh/id_", @"\.kube\config", @"application_default_credentials.json")
| project CredTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.github.com","uploads.github.com")
| join kind=inner creds on DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId
| where Timestamp between (CredTime .. CredTime + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, CredTime
| order by Timestamp desc
let creds = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe)?$"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)(\.aws[\\/]credentials|\.ssh[\\/]id_|\.kube[\\/]config|application_default_credentials\.json)"
| project CredTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where Url has_any ("api.github.com","uploads.github.com")
| where HttpMethod in ("POST","PUT")
| join kind=inner creds on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (CredTime .. CredTime + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestBodyBytes, CredTime
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\npm.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe) @DestinationHostname:(api.github.com OR uploads.github.com OR raw.githubusercontent.com)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(api|uploads)\.github\.com|raw\.githubusercontent\.com/i ContextImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| _count > 3
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.app) as app min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") AND (All_Traffic.dest="api.github.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="uploads.github.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="raw.githubusercontent.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where count > 5 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(All_Traffic.dest) as dest values(All_Traffic.app) as app min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") AND (All_Traffic.dest="api.github.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="uploads.github.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="raw.githubusercontent.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where count > 5 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Bling Libra: Entra device join immediately after vishing-driven MFA registration AIInstallation High
Detects Bling Libra's (ShinyHunters / UNC6040) post-vishing persistence pattern — within minutes of a successful interactive sign-in from a new location/IP, the same identity registers a new device (and frequently a new MFA method) on Entra ID. The article confirms the playbook is unchanged: vishing → credential+MFA intercept → register own device for persistence. Rationale: Article states Bling Libra 'continues to use vishing for initial access… and ultimately registering their own devices to establish persistence within targeted environments.' Mandiant/Google Cloud and BankInfoSecurity writeups confirm device-registration-within-30-minutes-of-suspicious-sign-in as the high-fidelity correlation. The temporal join is what distinguishes attacker registration from a user's own new laptop enrollment. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/defense-against-shinyhunters-cybercrime-saas • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/expansion-shinyhunters-saas-data-theft • https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/hanging-up-on-shinyhunters-experts-detail-vishing-defenses-a-30657
ATT&CKT1556.006 T1098.005 T1566.004
Data sourcesAuthentication Change
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine new-hire onboarding enrolling laptop+phone in a single session
  • User getting a new corporate laptop and enrolling from the IT helpdesk's external IP
  • Traveling exec signing in from a hotel and enrolling their iPad
  • Conditional Access compliant-device evaluation triggering re-registration
  • Autopilot device join from a freshly-imaged endpoint over a public Wi-Fi
Suppression filter
| where not (SignInIP in (dynamic(["<corp-helpdesk-egress-ip>","<onboarding-vlan-ip>"]))) and not (AppDisplayName has_any ("Microsoft Intune","Windows Autopilot"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: in Entra portal pull the registered device's join type (AzureAD, Hybrid), OS, and trust state; cross-check the registering IP against the user's normal locations (last 90d sign-in geo); ask the user (out-of-band, NOT via email — vishing actor may be monitoring inbox) whether they enrolled. 2) Contain: in Entra disable the new device object, revoke all refresh tokens for the user (`Revoke-MgUserSignInSession`), force password reset and re-MFA registration, block the source IP via CA named-location. 3) Hunt: pivot on AppDisplayName/ResourceDisplayName the same identity touched in the next 24h (Salesforce, Snowflake, Workday — Bling Libra's typical SaaS targets); query MailItemsAccessed for forwarding rules; look for OAuth app consents granted from the new device.
let lookback = 7d;
let signins = AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where IsInteractive == true
| where RiskLevelDuringSignIn in ("medium","high") or RiskState == "atRisk" or NetworkLocationDetails !has "trustedNamedLocation"
| project SignInTime=Timestamp, AccountUpn, SignInIP=IPAddress, SignInCountry=Country, AppDisplayName;
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where Application == "Office 365" or ApplicationId == 11161
| where ActionType in ("Add device","Add registered owner to device","Update device","Register device")
| extend Upn = tostring(AccountDisplayName)
| join kind=inner signins on $left.AccountObjectId == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (SignInTime .. SignInTime + 30m)
| project Timestamp, SignInTime, DelaySec=datetime_diff('second',Timestamp,SignInTime), AccountDisplayName, SignInIP, SignInCountry, IPAddress, ActionType, ObjectName, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 7d;
let signins = SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ResultType == 0
| where IsInteractive == true
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion)
| where RiskLevelDuringSignIn in ("medium","high") or RiskState == "atRisk" or isnotempty(Country)
| project SignInTime=TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, SignInIP=IPAddress, Country, AppDisplayName;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where LoggedByService in ("Device Registration Service","Core Directory")
| where OperationName in ("Add device","Add registered owner to device","Register device","Update device")
| where Result == "success"
| extend Upn = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)
| extend AuditIP = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend TargetDevice = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| join kind=inner signins on $left.Upn == $right.UserPrincipalName
| where TimeGenerated between (SignInTime .. SignInTime + 30m)
| project TimeGenerated, SignInTime, DelaySec=datetime_diff('second',TimeGenerated,SignInTime), Upn, SignInIP, Country, AuditIP, OperationName, TargetDevice
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Add device" OR "Add registered owner to device" OR "Register device") @properties.result:success

Hazy Scorpius (CL0P) Oracle EBS exploitation via CVE-2025-61882 — concurrent processing spawns shell/wget AIExploitation High
Hunts the post-exploit footprint of CVE-2025-61882 in Oracle E-Business Suite (Concurrent Processing) — the Java app-server process (java/oracle) spawning OS shells, wget, curl, perl or python is the canonical Cl0p webshell-drop pattern observed by Mandiant/Google Cloud against EBS 12.2.x. Rationale: Article names CVE-2025-61882 as Hazy Scorpius/CL0P's vector into Oracle EBS. Google Cloud TI and Oracle's own advisory confirm Cl0p drops Java/JSP webshells via the Concurrent Processing component; java/FNDLIBR spawning a shell/downloader on an EBS host is the cleanest live-exploit pivot. Filter for EBS-specific paths (appsutil, FMW_Home, comn/util) keeps this scoped to actual EBS servers. Cross-checked against: • https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/alert-cve-2025-61882.html • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/oracle-ebusiness-suite-zero-day-exploitation • https://www.tenable.com/blog/cve-2025-61882-faq-oracle-e-business-suite-zero-day-cl0p-and-july-2025-cpu • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2025-61882-critical-0day-in-oracle-e-business-suite-exploited-in-the-wild/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Oracle EBS patching (adop / adcfgclone / autoconfig) spawning bash to run admin scripts
  • Concurrent programs (custom XML Publisher reports) that legitimately exec wget to pull data
  • DBA running adstrtal.sh / adstpall.sh start-stop scripts via java wrapper
  • Backup scripts (RMAN wrappers) launched by FNDLIBR cron
  • Monitoring agents (Oracle Enterprise Manager) shelling out for OS metric collection
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("adstrtal","adstpall","adcfgclone","adop","autoconfig","rman","emagent")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "AutoPatch"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm patch level — Oracle's October 2025 CPU patches CVE-2025-61882; if unpatched, assume exploitation. Pull the full child-process tree and any files written in the last 24h under $APPL_TOP, $COMMON_TOP, /tmp; grep web/app logs for the IOC IPs in Oracle's advisory. Hash any new .jsp/.class files in $OA_HTML. 2) Contain: take the EBS app server out of load-balancer rotation, snapshot for forensics, then apply the CPU patch + remove any webshells under $OA_HTML / FMW_Home/user_projects. Rotate all DB credentials, APPS schema password, WLS admin password. 3) Hunt: search egress logs for connections to the published Cl0p IOC IPs (Oracle advisory + Mandiant blog); check for compressed exfil archives under /tmp, /var/tmp, $LOG_HOME; review CL0P leak site for victim listing if exfil suspected.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","java.exe","FNDLIBR","FNDLIBR.exe","httpd","httpd.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("oracle","EBS","fs_inst","appsutil","FMW_Home","comn/util","Concurrent")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","ksh","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wget","curl","perl","python","python3","nc","ncat","certutil.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "adstrtal" and ProcessCommandLine !has "adstpall"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(java|java\.exe|FNDLIBR|httpd)(\.exe)?$"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(oracle|EBS|fs_inst|appsutil|FMW_Home|comn/util|Concurrent)"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(sh|bash|ksh|zsh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe|wget|curl|perl|python3?|nc|ncat|certutil\.exe)$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !has "adstrtal" and ActingProcessCommandLine !has "adstpall"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:

let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)

SecurityEvent

Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI Secretly Steals Your AI Tokens

Aikido
2026-05-27 11 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A polished Codex remote UI, the npm package codexui-android, has active development and thousands of weekly users. It has been quietly exfiltrating OpenAI auth tokens for the past month. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1528 T1555.003
Domainssentry.anyclaw.store anyclaw.store gyx.com
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
Phase 1
Reconnaissance

Weaponization

Exploitation
