Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.005 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("74.125.202.103", "142.251.183.138", "173.194.193.138", "173.194.206.106", "178.156.177.192", "191.101.131.250", "195.160.221.203", "104.21.64.137", "173.194.194.94", "191.96.224.87", "191.96.225.241", "191.96.78.172", "191.96.78.28", "191.96.79.133", "191.96.79.179", "191.96.79.41", "192.178.209.95", "200.9.155.153", "74.125.132.95", "78.135.93.123", "79.133.57.141") or RemoteUrl has_any ("arbsniper.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,

let BadDomains = dynamic(["arbsniper.com"]);
ImNetworkSession

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical

Laravel-Lang supply chain C2/exfil to flipboxstudio.info AICommand & Control High
Hunts DNS lookups, SNI, or HTTP host headers to flipboxstudio[.]info — the C2/exfil domain used by the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer package compromise. The domain hosts both /payload (second-stage) and /exfil (stolen secrets), so any traffic to it from a Laravel-running host or CI runner indicates active compromise. Rationale: flipboxstudio[.]info is the single attacker-controlled C2/exfil endpoint named in the Snyk advisory and corroborated by StepSecurity, The Hacker News, Socket and Cyberpress. The domain has no legitimate use, so any successful resolution or connection is high-fidelity. Hits both DNS and HTTP/SNI telemetry to catch the resolution even if the payload connection is blocked. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/laravel-lang-php-packages-compromised.html • https://socket.dev/blog/laravel-lang-compromise • https://github.com/Laravel-Lang/http-statuses/issues/277
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1195.002
Data sourcesWeb Network_Resolution Network_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel feed ingestion tools or sandbox detonators resolving the IOC for enrichment (e.g. urlscan.io workers, VirusTotal retrohunts)
  • Security researchers manually browsing the indicator from a corporate workstation
  • Brand-protection / takedown vendors fetching the domain for evidence
  • DNS sinkhole or honeypot infrastructure replaying the IOC
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("urlscan-worker.exe","vt-fetch.exe") and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("threat-intel-svc","sandbox-detonator")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the resolving host and the initiating process; pull DeviceProcessEvents for the same DeviceId at ±10min to see if PHP (php-fpm, php.exe, artisan, composer) or cscript.exe is the parent. If the host runs Laravel, treat as confirmed. 2) Contain: sinkhole flipboxstudio[.]info at egress proxy/DNS, isolate the host with EDR, rotate every credential that ever touched it (AWS/GCP/Azure profile files, kubeconfigs, Vault tokens, CI/CD tokens, SSH keys, .env values, browser-stored creds, password vaults, crypto wallets, Slack/Discord/Telegram tokens). 3) Hunt: enumerate every project's composer.lock for laravel-lang/lang, laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/attributes, laravel-lang/actions; cross-reference with UC5 file-hunt; review egress logs for the domain across all CI/CD runners and staging environments.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "flipboxstudio.info" or RemoteUrl endswith "flipboxstudio.info"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has "flipboxstudio.info"
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has "flipboxstudio.info" or RequestURL has "flipboxstudio.info"
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Name=DestinationHostName, QueryType=RequestMethod, ResultCode=tostring(EventOutcome)),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has "flipboxstudio.info"
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Computer=SrcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, ResultCode=DnsResponseCodeName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Laravel-Lang stealer file drop in .laravel_locale temp directory AIInstallation High
Hunts file creation under any .laravel_locale subdirectory of a temp path. The Snyk advisory documents three artifacts under <tmp>/.laravel_locale/: an md5-hashed infection marker, a 12-hex-char .php second-stage stealer, and (on Windows) an 8-hex-char .vbs launcher. The directory name is unique to this campaign and has no benign use. Rationale: The Snyk IOC table explicitly names <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<md5>, <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<12 hex>.php, and <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 hex>.vbs as stealer artifacts; StepSecurity corroborates the /tmp staging behaviour. The directory string is unique to this campaign and matches regardless of whether tmp resolves to /tmp, $TMPDIR, or %TEMP%. The filename regex extensions tag which stage fired for fast triage. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://socket.dev/blog/laravel-lang-compromise
ATT&CKT1059 T1105 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate package or internal tool coincidentally named .laravel_locale (none known)
  • DFIR analyst staging recovered artifacts into a folder for analysis
  • Backup software restoring a previously-infected host's temp directory
  • Container image build caching a directory of that name
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("backup-restore.exe","veeam.backup.shell.exe","7z.exe","tar.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("restore","extract","unzip"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the directory contents and the InitiatingProcessFileName/CommandLine — expect php (php-fpm, php-cgi, php.exe, artisan, queue:work) as the writer. Hash any .php/.vbs found and look up against AlienVault/VT. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the writing process tree, preserve the directory for forensics before any cleanup script runs (the stealer self-deletes). Rotate all credentials reachable from that host. 3) Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessFileName + AccountName for all hosts that wrote .laravel_locale in the last 30d, then check each for outbound traffic to flipboxstudio[.]info (UC1) and presence of vendor/laravel-lang/*/src/helpers.php (UC5).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has ".laravel_locale"
| extend Marker = iff(FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{32}$", "infection_marker", "")
| extend Stage2 = iff(FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{12}\.php$", "stealer_php", "")
| extend VbsLauncher = iff(FileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{8}\.vbs$", "vbs_launcher", "")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, Marker, Stage2, VbsLauncher, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has ".laravel_locale"
| extend Marker = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{32}$", "infection_marker", "")
| extend Stage2 = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{12}\.php$", "stealer_php", "")
| extend VbsLauncher = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"^[a-f0-9]{8}\.vbs$", "vbs_launcher", "")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, Marker, Stage2, VbsLauncher
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Laravel-Lang Stealer Drop in .laravel_locale Temp Directory
id: 7c9d1e4f-2b34-5a8e-bd9c-2345678901bc
description: Detects file creation under a .laravel_locale subdirectory in any temp path - the staging location of the May 2026 Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain stealer (infection marker, 12-hex .php stage-2, 8-hex .vbs launcher).
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains: '.laravel_locale'
  condition: selection
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\.laravel_locale\* OR *\.LARAVEL_LOCALE\*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @file.path:(*/.laravel_locale/* OR */.LARAVEL_LOCALE/*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.laravel_locale[\\\/]/i
| TargetFileName=/(\.laravel_locale[\\\/](?<artifact>[a-f0-9]{32}|[a-f0-9]{12}\.php|[a-f0-9]{8}\.vbs)$)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as procs from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.laravel_locale/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.laravel_locale\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

DebugChromium.exe execution (Laravel-Lang stealer Windows artifact) AIInstallation High
Hunts execution of DebugChromium.exe anywhere on disk. The Snyk advisory names this binary as a Windows artifact observed on hosts infected by the Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain stealer. The name impersonates a Chrome debug build to blend in with developer tooling; there is no legitimate Microsoft/Google binary by this name. Rationale: DebugChromium.exe is called out by name in the Snyk IOC table as a Windows artifact observed on infected hosts. The string is unique - no legitimate Microsoft or Google product ships a binary by this name - so a process-create on this filename is essentially confirmation of infection. Captures parent (likely cscript.exe from UC4) for chain reconstruction. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/ • https://securityonline.info/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack-rce-backdoor/
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1204.002 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer naming a personal Chromium debug build DebugChromium.exe (uncommon — Chromium devs use chrome.exe or content_shell.exe)
  • Red-team operator re-using the IOC name in an authorised exercise
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonating the sample on a corporate analyst VM
Response runbook
1) Triage: collect SHA256 of the image and compare against the StepSecurity/Snyk hash list. Identify parent — UC4 will show cscript.exe from %TEMP%\.laravel_locale as the spawner. Pull DeviceNetworkEvents for the same DeviceId to confirm UC1 traffic. 2) Contain: isolate host with EDR, kill the process tree, quarantine the binary, rotate every credential cached or used on the host. 3) Hunt: search the file across the fleet using SHA256 from the first hit (DeviceFileEvents), and pivot on InitiatingProcessParentFileName to find the originating Laravel/CI process.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "DebugChromium.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\DebugChromium.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

cscript/wscript executing a script from .laravel_locale temp directory AIInstallation High
Hunts cscript.exe or wscript.exe invocations whose command line references a .laravel_locale path. The Snyk advisory describes the Windows execution chain as the malicious PHP helper writing an 8-hex-char .vbs into %TEMP%\.laravel_locale\ and launching it via cscript — pairing the canonical script interpreter with the stealer's unique staging directory yields a tight signal. Rationale: Snyk explicitly documents the Windows execution chain as a .vbs launcher under %TEMP%\.laravel_locale\. The compound (cscript|wscript) + .laravel_locale leaves no realistic benign matches — neither Windows nor any common dev tool stages scripts in a directory of that name. Captures parent process so triage shows the PHP runtime (php.exe / php-cgi) that originated the launch. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack • https://snyk.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-advisory/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1218 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DFIR replay of recovered samples in a sandbox folder reusing the name
  • Red-team exercise replicating the IOC for control validation
  • Backup software temporarily extracting a previously-infected host into a similarly-named directory
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("backup-restore.exe","7z.exe","explorer.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("restore","extract","unzip"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture full CommandLine (the .vbs path will be embedded), the parent (expect php.exe / php-cgi.exe / artisan when fresh), and confirm InitiatingProcessParentFileName. Hash the .vbs from disk before the stealer self-deletes. 2) Contain: kill the cscript process tree, isolate the host, quarantine the .vbs and DebugChromium.exe (UC3). Rotate all credentials reachable from the host. 3) Hunt: pivot the parent process's user/host across DeviceFileEvents for vendor\laravel-lang\*\src\helpers.php (UC5) and DeviceNetworkEvents for flipboxstudio.info (UC1) to confirm the full chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("cscript.exe","wscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".laravel_locale"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\wscript.exe"
| where CommandLine has ".laravel_locale"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Compromised laravel-lang Composer package: helpers.php in vendor tree AIDelivery High
Hunts the file write or presence of src/helpers.php under vendor/laravel-lang/{lang,http-statuses,attributes,actions}/. A legitimate localization package has no reason to ship an autoload-files helper, so any host whose Composer cache contains this file pulled a poisoned tag during the May 22-23 2026 incident and should be treated as compromised until the package is rolled back and credentials rotated. Rationale: The Snyk detection guidance explicitly tells defenders to inspect vendor/laravel-lang/*/ for the presence of src/helpers.php — legitimate releases of these four localization packages do not ship a helpers file or use autoload.files. The package-name regex narrows to the four named-compromised packages (lang, http-statuses, attributes, actions) per the affected-versions table, avoiding stray matches on other laravel-lang/* repos. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/Laravel-Lang/http-statuses/issues/277 • https://gbhackers.com/compromise-laravel-lang-packages/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/laravel-lang-supply-chain-attack
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Forensic image mount where an analyst is reviewing a known-compromised host's vendor tree
  • Repo of pinned/known-bad samples kept for red-team or detection-engineering validation
  • Backup-restore of an older Laravel project that legitimately had a custom helpers.php (rare — the path /vendor/laravel-lang/<pkg>/src/ is vendor-managed, devs shouldn't write there)
  • Internal fork of a laravel-lang package that genuinely adds a helpers file (audit composer.json autoload.files to confirm intent)
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the actual helpers.php content and composer.json on the host — confirm autoload.files registers it and the contents include an HTTP fetch to flipboxstudio[.]info. Pull composer.lock to record the exact poisoned version+integrity hash. 2) Contain: roll back to a known-good pinned version after Packagist relists (or vendor a clean local fork), invalidate Composer cache (composer clearcache + delete vendor/), rebuild and redeploy. Rotate every credential the affected runtime could have touched: AWS/GCP/Azure profiles, kubeconfigs, Vault tokens, CI/CD secrets, SSH keys, .env values, browser sessions, password manager vaults, crypto wallets, Slack/Discord/Telegram tokens. 3) Hunt: chain to UC1 (flipboxstudio.info egress) and UC2 (.laravel_locale temp drops) on the same DeviceId/runner to determine if the second-stage actually executed and exfiltrated. Search every CI/CD job log and container image registry for vendor/laravel-lang/*/src/helpers.php to find untracked compromis
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "vendor\\laravel-lang\\" or FolderPath has "vendor/laravel-lang/"
| where FileName =~ "helpers.php"
| extend Package = extract(@"laravel-lang[\\/](lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)", 1, FolderPath)
| where isnotempty(Package)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, Package, SHA256, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "vendor/laravel-lang/" or TargetFilePath has @"vendor\laravel-lang\"
| where TargetFileName =~ "helpers.php"
| extend Package = extract(@"laravel-lang[\\/](lang|http-statuses|attributes|actions)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where isnotempty(Package)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Package, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or SHA1 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or MD5 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or SHA1 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375") or MD5 in~ ("bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["bba2e443dc7ff1f8704f52a5375383e3f4f643b8", "a5ea2e8fa92ccf29cdb1d2dadbeb27722b2bff37", "556d2b335d4d6d92139822017ee461b668afe375"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Composer install of malicious helpers.php in laravel-lang vendor package
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages with Credential Stealer
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] cscript.exe launching .vbs from .laravel_locale temp directory · [LLM] Stealer or VBS launcher dropped into .laravel_locale temp directory · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 egress to flipboxstudio.info from Laravel-Lang composer dropper · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
C2 egress to flipboxstudio.info from Laravel-Lang composer dropper AICommand & Control High
Detects any HTTP/DNS contact with the hard-coded C2 domain flipboxstudio.info (decoded from integer array in the malicious src/helpers.php). Both the /payload fetch (stage-2 stealer download) and /exfil (AES-256 encrypted credential exfil) hit the same FQDN, so any resolution or connection is unambiguously malicious. Rationale: Anchored on the article's named C2 domain flipboxstudio.info plus the /payload and /exfil URL paths quoted verbatim. Corroborated by https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities and https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/malicious-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1132.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / threat-intel analyst sandboxing the IOC from a corp endpoint
  • DNS over HTTPS resolver pre-fetching from threat-feed subscriptions
  • Aikido/Snyk/Socket scanning engine on a build agent verifying the IOC
  • Legacy reference to defunct flipboxstudio brand if same FQDN was previously legitimate (verify WHOIS dates)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("aikido-scanner.exe","socket-cli.exe","snyk.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--threat-intel","--ioc-validate"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on DeviceName/SourceIP — pull the initiating process. cscript.exe launching .vbs from .laravel_locale temp directory AIInstallation High
Detects the Windows arm of the Laravel-Lang dropper: the malicious src/helpers.php writes an 8-hex-character .vbs launcher into <temp>\.laravel_locale\ and executes it silently via cscript. Process tree is php/php-fpm/php-cgi (or anything that triggered composer autoload) → cscript.exe with a .vbs path containing `.laravel_locale`. Rationale: Anchored on two article-quoted strings together: `<tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 random hex chars>.vbs` and the explicit `runs the payload silently via cscript` Windows-launcher behaviour. The 8-hex regex makes this near-zero-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://gbhackers.com/malicious-laravel-packages/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1105 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer reproducing the IOC in a sandbox (would show non-php parent)
  • Security tool / sandbox detonating sample with reused .laravel_locale path naming
  • Internal red-team exercise replaying the dropper
  • Unrelated legitimate VBS in a folder coincidentally containing the substring '.laravel_locale' (extremely unlikely given path-component anchoring)
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull full process tree — confirm parent is php.exe / php-cgi.exe / php-fpm / composer.phar / cmd spawning composer; capture SHA256 of the .vbs and any dropped .php in same dir. 2) Contain: kill cscript chain, isolate host, snapshot <tmp>\.laravel_locale\ for forensics, block flipboxstudio.info. 3) Hunt: cross-reference DeviceFileEvents for any .php files written to .laravel_locale on this host (the 5,900-line stealer), enumerate cloud/SSH/browser/crypto creds present on the host and rotate immediately; pivot to other dev workstations with same composer.lock entries for laravel-lang/lang/attributes/http-statuses.
let LookbackDays = 14d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "cscript.exe" or FileName =~ "wscript.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has @".laravel_locale"
   and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 14d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
  SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith "\\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\wscript.exe"
  | where CommandLine has ".laravel_locale" and CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
),
(
  ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has ".laravel_locale"
     and ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\.laravel_locale[\\\\/][0-9a-f]{8}\.vbs"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Composer install of malicious helpers.php in laravel-lang vendor package AIDelivery Medium
Detects composer (or any file mover) writing a src/helpers.php file under vendor/laravel-lang/{lang,attributes,http-statuses}/ — the article confirms this file does not exist in the legitimate packages and was injected by the attacker via fork-tag commits. Catches the supply-chain payload at composer-install time, before the dropper detonates. Rationale: Anchored on the article-quoted file name (`src/helpers.php`) plus the three affected package names verbatim (`laravel-lang/lang`, `laravel-lang/attributes`, `laravel-lang/http-statuses`). The file is novel to the malicious tags, so any write is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://socket.dev/blog/malicious-packagist-packages-disguised-as-laravel-utilities • https://thehackernews.com/2026/03/fake-laravel-packages-on-packagist.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer re-pulling a cleaned/patched laravel-lang version that legitimately ships helpers.php in a future release
  • Forensic restore of a known-bad artifact from backup for IR analysis
  • Composer cache deduplication tools copying the file between projects
  • Container-image rebuild that includes a pinned malicious version still present in composer.lock
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the parent process (expect composer.phar / php composer / docker build / CI runner). Pull SHA256 of the dropped helpers.php and search for the strings `laravel_lang_locale`, `laravel_lang_fallback`, `flipboxstudio` or integer-array C2 encoding inside the file. 2) Contain: delete the vendor/laravel-lang/ directory; pin composer.json to a known-good pre-attack version (or remove these packages entirely); re-run composer install; block flipboxstudio.info at the perimeter. 3) Hunt: if the file appears, treat the host as compromised — rotate every credential reachable from it (AWS/GCP/Azure keys, EC2 IMDS role, kubeconfig, SSH keys, .git-credentials, GitHub/GitLab CLI tokens, browser saved passwords, crypto wallet seeds, Slack/Discord/Telegram bot tokens, VPN creds); pivot to all other workstations/CI runners sharing the same composer.lock.
let LookbackDays = 30d;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "helpers.php"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)[\\\\/]vendor[\\\\/]laravel-lang[\\\\/](lang|attributes|http-statuses)[\\\\/]src[\\\\/]?$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "helpers.php"
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)[\\\\/]vendor[\\\\/]laravel-lang[\\\\/](lang|attributes|http-statuses)[\\\\/]src[\\\\/]helpers\.php$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256

| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access

    category: file_access
    product: windows

    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'

        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'

            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'

level: high

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Megalodon backdoor workflow file (SysDiag.yml / Optimize-Build.yml) written to .github/workflows/ · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Megalodon: Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration Across 5,500+ Public Reposito
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Megalodon CI/CD exfil: outbound HTTPS to C2 216.126.225.129:8443 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Megalodon harvester: curl POST to C2 /collect endpoint on Linux runner · [LLM] Megalodon harvester: bash secret-grep across workspace (API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA) · [LLM] Megalodon harvester: clustered read of ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json in one session · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Megalodon CI/CD exfil: outbound HTTPS to C2 216.126.225.129:8443 AICommand & Control Medium
Detects any host (corporate proxy, EDR-monitored endpoint, self-hosted GitHub Actions runner) initiating a connection to the Megalodon campaign C2 server. The IP/port pair is unique to this campaign and any hit is a near-certain compromise indicator across the org. Rationale: Anchors on the article-published C2 IP 216.126.225.129 — a single hard IOC that StepSecurity attributes directly to the Megalodon campaign. The IP/port combo is not associated with any legitimate service in the article and any internal egress is high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1041 T1567 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red team or IR analyst replaying the IOC for validation
  • Threat-intel platform performing IP reputation/sandbox lookups against the IOC
  • Honeypot or deception infrastructure deliberately calling the IOC to log adversary follow-on
  • CTI researcher in the org pivoting on the IP via VirusTotal/Shodan from a workstation
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("VirusTotalUploader.exe","sandboxie.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--ir-validation"
Response runbook
Triage: pivot DeviceName/SourceIP back to its role — is this a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner, developer workstation that cloned a poisoned repo, or production workload? Pull initiating process and command line; expected pattern is curl POST to /collect. Contain: block 216.126.225.129/32 at egress firewall and proxy; isolate the device in Defender/CrowdStrike; rotate ALL secrets potentially present on the runner (cloud IAM keys, OIDC trust relationships, npm tokens, SSH keys, GitHub PATs, Vault tokens). Treat OIDC token exposure as full cloud-role compromise — re-scope or delete trust policies. Hunt: pivot off the device to UC3 (mass secret grep), UC5 (cred-file fan-out), and search GitHub audit logs for commits authored by build-bot@github-ci.com or ci-pipeline@actions-bot.com on any repo the org owns.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "216.126.225.129"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where DestinationIP == "216.126.225.129"
   | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceAction),
  (ImNetworkSession
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where DstIpAddr == "216.126.225.129"
   | project TimeGenerated, Vendor=EventVendor, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, SourceHostName=SrcHostname, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=DstPortNumber, RequestURL=Url, DeviceAction=DvcAction)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Megalodon harvester: curl POST to C2 /collect endpoint on Linux runner AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the runtime exfil step of the Megalodon payload — a curl invocation POSTing gzipped credential blob to https://216.126.225.129:8443/collect. Catches both self-hosted runners and any Linux/Windows host re-executing the decoded payload. Rationale: Pivots on the verbatim exfil command in the article — curl POST to https://216.126.225.129:8443/collect with --data-binary. Combining curl binary + IP + /collect path makes a near-zero-FP detection that catches the payload even if the decoded bash is split across multiple invocations.
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1041 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR/red-team replaying the public payload on a test runner
  • Reverse-engineer detonating the decoded bash in a sandbox
  • Detection-engineering validation test in non-prod
  • Threat-intel scraper fetching the exact URL
Response runbook
Triage: confirm process tree — initiating bash should be child of a GitHub Actions Runner.Listener / runsvc.sh / runner-worker process for a self-hosted runner, or any sh/bash on a non-runner host. Inspect ProcessCommandLine for the full curl argv (`-X POST`, `--data-binary @-`). Contain: kill the curl PID, isolate host, block 216.126.225.129/32 egress. If a GitHub Actions runner: deregister the runner, revoke its registration token, and rotate the repo/org-level PAT and any OIDC trust relationships exposed. Hunt: same aid/DeviceName — look for preceding bash with base64 -d piping into bash, env dump, ~/.ssh/id_* reads (UC5), and grep with API_KEY/SECRET/TOKEN pattern (UC3). Cross-check GitHub for recent workflow file changes on the repo whose runner fired.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "curl" or FileName =~ "curl.exe" or FolderPath endswith "/curl"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "216.126.225.129" and ProcessCommandLine has "/collect"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "curl" or ActingProcessName endswith "curl.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "216.126.225.129" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/collect"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Megalodon harvester: bash secret-grep across workspace (API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the recursive secret-scrape step of the Megalodon payload — `grep -rE "(API_KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|PRIVATE_KEY|BEGIN RSA)"` walking the CI checkout looking for hardcoded secrets. The literal token list is the article-published payload string. Rationale: All six tokens (API_KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, PRIVATE_KEY, BEGIN RSA) appear verbatim in the published bash payload's grep regex. Requiring all six together discriminates Megalodon from generic secret-scanners (gitleaks/trufflehog use their own ruleset, not raw greps with this exact token list).
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ad-hoc developer secret-audit shell one-liners
  • Custom in-house secret-scanning script using this exact pattern
  • Security training/CTF exercises using this canonical pattern
  • Pre-commit hooks running grep-based secret scans
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("gitleaks","trufflehog","detect-secrets","semgrep","ggshield") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("gitleaks","trufflehog","--baseline","pre-commit")
Response runbook
Triage: inspect parent process — is this running under a CI runner identity (e.g. `runner`, `gitlab-runner`, `dockerexec`), a service account on a build host, or an interactive user? Megalodon variant always spawns from base64-decoded bash under the runner-worker tree. Contain: if running on a CI runner, terminate the job and deregister the runner. Rotate every secret accessible to that pipeline (cloud IAM, npm tokens, GitHub PATs). Hunt: pivot on same aid/DeviceName for UC1 (egress to C2), UC2 (curl /collect), and UC5 (cred-file fan-out). Check upstream GitHub for recent workflow edits authored by build-bot@github-ci.com or ci-pipeline@actions-bot.com.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "grep" or FolderPath endswith "/grep"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("API_KEY", "SECRET", "TOKEN", "PASSWORD", "PRIVATE_KEY", "BEGIN RSA")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "grep"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("API_KEY", "SECRET", "TOKEN", "PASSWORD", "PRIVATE_KEY", "BEGIN RSA")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Megalodon backdoor workflow file (SysDiag.yml / Optimize-Build.yml) written to .github/workflows/ AIInstallation High
Detects creation of a workflow file with one of the two campaign-specific filenames inside any .github/workflows/ directory. Catches developer workstations that cloned/pulled a poisoned repository as well as self-hosted runners checking out the malicious tree. Rationale: Both filenames (SysDiag.yml, Optimize-Build.yml) and the `name:` field values SysDiag / Optimize-Build are called out as the two campaign variants in the article and the recommended GitHub code search anchors. The path scope (.github/workflows/) plus exact filename match make this near-zero-FP.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate project genuinely naming a workflow SysDiag.yml or Optimize-Build.yml — exceedingly rare
  • IR/red-team adding the IOC file to a test repo for detection validation
  • Threat-intel analyst pulling the SafeDep megalodon-campaign-commits.csv reference repo locally
Response runbook
Triage: inspect the file content — confirm the workflow `name:` field is SysDiag or Optimize-Build and the run block contains a base64 blob piped to bash. Cross-reference the repo against SafeDep's megalodon-campaign-commits.csv. Contain: alert the repo owner; revert the malicious commit via `git revert <sha>`; force-pull a clean copy and require branch-protection with mandatory PR reviews on the default branch. If the workflow ever ran on a self-hosted runner, treat all secrets and OIDC trust relationships exposed to that runner as compromised. Hunt: search all org repos for the same two filenames and for commits authored by build-bot@github-ci.com / ci-pipeline@actions-bot.com with messages 'ci: add build optimization step' / 'chore: optimize pipeline runtime' / 'chore: update ci/cd pipeline'.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has ".github\\workflows" or FolderPath has ".github/workflows"
| where FileName in~ ("SysDiag.yml","Optimize-Build.yml")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has ".github/workflows" or TargetFilePath has ".github\\workflows"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("SysDiag.yml","Optimize-Build.yml")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Megalodon harvester: clustered read of ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json in one session AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the credential-collection fan-out pattern — a single process tree reading multiple distinct credential stores (SSH private key, kube config, npm token, Docker registry creds) within a one-minute window. Catches Megalodon even if the bash one-liner is split into separate cat invocations and the C2 IP is not yet contactable. Rationale: Anchors directly on the article's decoded payload (Code blocks 2 and 3) — the exact targets cat'd by the Megalodon harvester: /proc/1/environ, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json. Requiring ≥3 distinct targets from the same parent within 1 minute discriminates from any single legitimate dotfile-reading tool.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible/Chef/Puppet provisioning role enumerating user credentials
  • Container-image bake script copying user dotfiles into an image
  • Backup agent (restic, borg) walking $HOME
  • Developer running `dotfiles install` or similar bootstrap script
  • Kubernetes/cloud SDK install scripts merging multiple credential files
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible-playbook","puppet","chef-client","salt-call","restic","borg","rsync") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("ansible","--inventory","site.pp","chef-solo")
Response runbook
Triage: identify parent process. Megalodon harvester runs under a child of the GitHub Actions runner-worker (Runner.Worker / runsvc.sh) or under a base64-decoded bash. A legitimate config-management tool will run as ansible/puppet/chef child of cron or sshd. Contain: if on a CI runner, terminate the job, deregister the runner, rotate all secrets in scope of the pipeline. Rotate SSH keys read; revoke npm tokens; cycle kube config service-account tokens; rotate Docker registry creds. Hunt: pivot on same DeviceName for UC1 (egress to 216.126.225.129) and UC2 (curl /collect). Look for preceding `bash -c "echo <base64> | base64 -d | bash"` invocation. Audit GitHub for matching workflow file additions in the org.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMin = 1m;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FileName =~ "cat" or FolderPath endswith "/cat"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/1/environ","/.ssh/id_","/.kube/config","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json")
| extend Target = case(
    ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/1/environ","pid1_env",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.ssh/id_","ssh_key",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.kube/config","kube",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.npmrc","npm",
    ProcessCommandLine has "/.docker/config.json","docker",
    "")
| summarize
    DistinctTargets = dcount(Target),
    Targets = make_set(Target, 10),
    SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
    LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
    by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowMin = 1m;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "cat"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/1/environ","/.ssh/id_","/.kube/config","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json")
| extend Target = case(
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/1/environ","pid1_env",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.ssh/id_","ssh_key",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.kube/config","kube",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.npmrc","npm",
    ActingProcessCommandLine has "/.docker/config.json","docker",
    "")
| summarize
    DistinctTargets = dcount(Target),
    Targets = make_set(Target, 10),
    SampleCmds = make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where DistinctTargets >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @process.executable.path:*\/cat @process.command_line:(*\/proc\/1\/environ* OR *\/.ssh\/id_* OR *\/.kube\/config* OR *\/.npmrc* OR *\/.docker\/config.json*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/cat$/i CommandLine=/(\/proc\/1\/environ|\/\.ssh\/id_|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json)/
| case {
    CommandLine=/\/proc\/1\/environ/ | target := "pid1";
    CommandLine=/\/\.ssh\/id_/ | target := "ssh";
    CommandLine=/\/\.kube\/config/ | target := "kube";
    CommandLine=/\/\.npmrc/ | target := "npm";
    CommandLine=/\/\.docker\/config\.json/ | target := "docker";
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(field=target, distinct=true, as=distinct_targets), collect([target])])
| distinct_targets >= 3
ENDPOINT

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
